'''Jerry Lee Atwood''' (born 1942) is an American supramolecular chemist. He is currently a Curators' Distinguished Professor in Chemistry at the [[University of Missouri]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Mizzou Alumni - 51st Annual Distinguished Faculty Award | date=2019 |url=https://www.mizzou.com/s/1002/alumni/interior.aspx?sid=1002&gid=1001&pgid=1386}}</ref> He is an international leader in Supramolecular chemistry. He has developed the field by his research and by writing a text book on Supramolecular Chemistry. <ref>{{citation|title=Wiley - Supramolecular Chemistry|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Supramolecular+Chemistry%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9780470512340|access-date=2018-01-23|archive-date=2019-12-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217133148/https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Supramolecular+Chemistry,+2nd+Edition-p-9780470512340|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education and early life==

Jerry Atwood was born in [[Springfield, Missouri]]. He attended [[Southwest Missouri State College]], graduating with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1964. He received his PhD from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1968.<ref>{{citation|title=Wiley - Supramolecular Chemistry|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Supramolecular+Chemistry%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9780470512340|access-date=2018-01-23|archive-date=2019-12-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217133148/https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Supramolecular+Chemistry,+2nd+Edition-p-9780470512340|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career and research==

Atwood was appointed as an assistant professor at the [[University of Alabama]] and was named a full professor in 1978. In 1994, he was appointed as a chair and professor in the department of chemistry with the [[University of Missouri]].<ref>{{citation|title=Wiley - Supramolecular Chemistry|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Supramolecular+Chemistry%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9780470512340|access-date=2018-01-23|archive-date=2019-12-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217133148/https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Supramolecular+Chemistry,+2nd+Edition-p-9780470512340|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

Atwood is a recipient of the most prestigious Izatt-Christensen International Macrocyclic Chemistry Award. He has also received an honorary [[doctor of science]] degree  from the [[University of South Florida]].<ref>{{citation |title= Commencement Scenes |url=http://news.usf.edu/article/templates/?a=5416&z=123}}</ref> Atwood also received an honor PREFACE from the [[ University of Georgia]]. <ref>{{citation|title= Honoring Professor Jerry Atwood Preface|url= http://www.chem.uga.edu/content/honoring-professor-jerry-l-atwood-preface|access-date= 2018-01-23|archive-date= 2018-03-15|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180315134045/http://www.chem.uga.edu/content/honoring-professor-jerry-l-atwood-preface|url-status= dead}}</ref>
